selection_rule: (deployed model may be overridden, see selection_details.override) highest mean out-of-fold balanced accuracy on the train split (all_features scenario), but Logistic Regression is kept unless the winner beats it by more than sampling noise (95% paired-bootstrap CI of the difference excludes 0)

override.reason: The statistical winner's advantage comes from fitting the step-like age pattern in the labels (an age-only model of the same type scores about the same as the all-feature model, and every model is at chance without age). That makes it a better reproducer of a suspect labelling artifact, not a better clinical predictor. The winner also gives no per-answer explanation and adds a heavy runtime dependency. The simpler, explainable Logistic Regression is deployed; use --deploy-model auto to deploy the rule's choice.

features.name: gender
features.description: Sex as recorded in the dataset (female/male).

features.name: body_weight
features.description: Derived from BMI by the frontend: underweight if BMI < 18.5, else normal.

excluded_columns.Hormonal Changes: not collected by CareMend; inconsistent with Gender in the data
excluded_columns.Race/Ethnicity: not collected by CareMend; no Indian category in the dataset
excluded_columns.Alcohol Consumption: valid ("None"/"Moderate") but only two levels, not a CareMend question in this form; ablation shows no reliable gain (see evaluation report)
excluded_columns.Medications: valid ("None"/"Corticosteroids"); ablation shows no reliable gain; CareMend does not ask for a medication list
excluded_columns.Medical Conditions: valid (None/Rheumatoid Arthritis/Hyperthyroidism); not collected by CareMend; ablation shows no reliable gain

decision_threshold_rule: highest specificity with train out-of-fold sensitivity >= 90%
score_semantics: raw model score in [0,1] = predict_proba of the positive class; UNCALIBRATED
calibration_note: Not justified: tiny sample and unverified labels. The score is only used to rank and to apply the decision threshold.

risk_categories.MEDIUM: not produced — a binary, uncalibrated model gives no defensible middle band

limitations: EXPERIMENTAL STUDENT PROJECT. Not clinically validated; not a diagnostic or treatment tool.
Trained on 1954 rows. Re-train on the full dataset before drawing any conclusion.
Label provenance is unverified: the file does not say how 'Osteoporosis' was determined (no DEXA/T-score).
Dataset representativeness for Indian users is unknown (Race/Ethnicity has no Indian category).
In the training data every record at or above age 39 is positive, so the model score is driven almost entirely by age; this pattern suggests synthetic or rule-generated labels.
Apart from age, the remaining features show little or no reliable predictive signal in this data (see evaluation report).
The score is NOT a calibrated probability and must not be read as 'x% chance of osteoporosis'.
A low score does not mean a person is free of osteoporosis. Only a DEXA scan and a clinician can assess bone health.
Body weight is derived from BMI (<18.5 = underweight, otherwise normal); the dataset has no 'overweight' category.
